findings.reason: the extractor's request/batch contract is the interface the node must implement, and the plan must state whether EQDB reuses `ChannelRequest` or adds a request type before the node can be dispatched.
findings.text: `RemoteEddbExtractor` and its batch framing are channel-shaped (`encode_batch` serialises `ChannelRequest(shot, category, dname)` and `write_channel` writes `(channel, time)`), but an EQDB record is psi on a 2-D grid with boundary and profiles; the plan asserts the EQDB read "keeps everything it already owns" and that "only the remote read call differs" while leaving the decoded record type to the open question `eqdb-reader` and saying nothing about the request encoding, so the public request contract change is unbudgeted and a node dispatched on this text cannot know whether it reuses or widens `ChannelRequest`

findings.reason: two independent readers of one SELENE equilibrium can drift in COCOS/axis handling, and the plan's own "one equilibrium has one shape" principle argues for a single SELENE source reader that both the sign scorer and the geometry referee adapt.
findings.text: §6 generalises the COCOS scorer so "the SELENE and FAME loaders each return an `EfitLabels`", and §7 separately "adds a SELENE reference loader and its firewall tier" reducing SELENE's psi/boundary/axis to `EquilibriumGeometry` for `read_efit_geometry`; that is two readers of the same facility equilibrium source into two typed records, with no owner named for the read

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the new modules hide substantial behaviour behind small interfaces (one `selene_deck.py` converter entry point, one `tokamap_export.py` function, one EQDB grid writer sharing `eddb.py` helpers), and the machine-keyed tables in the pin registry, identity registry and shot set extend three distinct existing owners rather than spreading a single mechanism across wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §6 and §7 add two separate readers of the same SELENE equilibrium (an `EfitLabels` loader for the COCOS scorer and an `EquilibriumGeometry` loader for `read_efit_geometry`), and the plan does not name the one that owns the SELENE read.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; each section that touches a family accounts for it in its own text (§2 and §5 "adds one data file and no public definition or refusal family"; §4 "widens one binding contract and retires nothing"; §7's `--machine` "replaces the implicit MAST default ... it retires nothing else"), so nothing is added without a stated retire/merge or a why-nothing-can-be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan names both codebases and the precise mechanisms it extends (`eddb.py`, `signal_map.py`, `transform_engine.py`, `cocos_convention.py`, `challenge/convention.py`, `efit_referee.py`, `artifact_resolution.py`, `machine_identity.py`, `spine_bench/shots.py`); each was opened and matches the plan's description.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §7 claims the EQDB read "extends" the channel-shaped extractor with "only the remote read call" differing, but `ChannelRequest(shot, category, dname)` cannot express a grid-equilibrium read and the plan never states whether the request contract widens or is overloaded.
